chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Marwān ibn Muslim and ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
What is between the hairline and the tip of the nose is the place of prostration; whichever part of that you make touch the ground will suffice you.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: it sufficed you, meaning it fulfilled the requirement
key_terms.أَصَبْتَ: you caused to touch or reach, referring to making that part touch the ground
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the ground, upon which sajdah is performed
key_terms.طَرَفِ الْأَنْفِ: the tip of the nose, marking the lower boundary mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.قُصَاصِ الشَّعْرِ: the hairline, marking the upper boundary of the forehead area for prostration
key_terms.مَسْجِدٌ: the place of prostration, meaning the area designated for sajdah

ai.seo_question: What part of the face must touch the ground in sajdah for it to be valid?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the area of the forehead relevant to sajdah, describing it as the space between the hairline and the tip of the nose. It indicates that if any part of that area touches the ground, the prostration is valid and sufficient.
